board: 7 columns a..g (left to right) x 6 rows 1..6 (row 1 at the bottom); pieces fall to the lowest empty cell of their column; four in a row horizontally, vertically or diagonally wins
encoding: cell index c = 6 * column + (row - 1), column a = 0 .. g = 6, so a1 = 0, a6 = 5, b1 = 6, g6 = 41; input c is 1 if x (the first player) has a piece on cell c, input 42 + c is 1 if o has one; an empty cell has both 0
dataset_facts: UCI Connect-4 (John Tromp, 1995): in its documentation's words, "all legal 8-ply positions in the game of connect-4 in which neither player has won yet, and in which the next move is not forced" (67,557 positions, 4 pieces each), each labelled with its game-theoretic value for the first player x under perfect play by both sides (x is to move: it is x's fifth move). Over all positions: win 65.8%, loss 24.6%, draw 9.5%. The held-out set is 1,000 positions of each value drawn at random.
forward: h1 = relu(fc1.weight @ x + fc1.bias); h2 = relu(fc2.weight @ h1 + fc2.bias); logits = fc3.weight @ h2 + fc3.bias; the prediction is the argmax (logits within 1e-9 x max(1, |max logit|) of the maximum count as tied; ties go to the lowest index)
metric: accuracy on the 3,000 held-out positions (1,000 per class, so accuracy is the mean of the three per-class recalls)
